claims.text: The as-cast (MnNiSi)0.62(FeCoGe)0.38 alloy has coarse grains.
The as-cast alloy is prone to cracking and has poor load-bearing integrity under operational conditions.
The as-cast alloy exhibits a large caloric response.
Rapid solidification will produce a fine, uniform grain structure in this alloy.
Annealing at approximately 400 °C for 1 hour under an inert atmosphere will relieve residual stresses.
The proposed short anneal will avoid significant grain coarsening.
The treatment will create a refined microstructure with a high density of grain boundaries.
The treatment may create nanoscale secondary-phase precipitates.
Grain boundaries and possible secondary-phase precipitates will deflect or blunt propagating cracks.
Grain refinement will hinder crack initiation and propagation and thereby improve toughness and load-bearing integrity.
The treatment will retain the crystallographic features and phase-transition behavior responsible for the caloric response.
Minimal thermal exposure during annealing will preserve caloric phase-transition characteristics.
Treated samples will have greater fracture toughness and a reduced tendency to crack relative to as-cast samples.
Treated samples will retain caloric performance close to that of the as-cast alloy under magnetic-field operation.
Treated samples will retain caloric performance close to that of the as-cast alloy under pressure-field operation.
The intervention is expected to be effective near ambient temperature, at typical caloric magnetic-field or pressure levels, and under service-representative mechanical loading.
